text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock fell 1.8% today, extending a steep two-week decline of 7.5%, amid a broader unraveling of the refinery-profit trade that has dominated energy stocks this year. The immediate trigger appears to be a CNBC headline explicitly stating "The biggest money-making energy trade looks over"—a signal that investors who piled into refiner stocks on the back of strong margins are now heading for the exits, regardless of today's specific operating conditions.

The refiner's fundamentals remain reasonably solid: refineries are running at 95.7% capacity and crude oil storage is elevated at 694 million barrels, which typically supports margins. However, geopolitical de-escalation in the Middle East (with Iran signaling openness to a U.S. deal) has reduced the premium that refinery stocks enjoyed from supply-disruption fears, while climate negotiations collapsing at COP31 may also be removing a bullish "energy transition scarcity" narrative that some investors had priced in. The market is rotating away from the sector as a whole, not reacting to anything broken about Marathon's business today.
